title: [bug] The firmware suite is red by design, so it cannot gate anything
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-23 at commit 7ed8ca2, in a clean worktree with the private fixtures symlinked:
./internal/multiplex/firmwaretests reports 25 FAILURES before any of that night's work. They are
almost all grid probes.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE COUNT. A suite this red cannot tell a regression from the status quo,
and that is not theoretical: a change to listings/1998-12-24.json moved the TV GUIDE menu's hash
and broke several probes, and establishing whether that was new required building a baseline
worktree and diffing failure sets by hand. That should be a glance at a green suite.

TWO DIFFERENT CAUSES, and they want different fixes:

1. PROBES THAT FAIL AS THEIR WAY OF REPORTING. A diagnostic that calls t.Fatal when it finds the
   thing it was built to find is a bug in the instrument. Two of that night's own probes did
   exactly this and were fixed (see "Make two probes report their findings instead of failing with
   them"): a finding gets ASSERTED -- so a change in either direction is news -- or LOGGED. It
   never gets reported as a broken harness.

2. PROBES PINNED TO SCREEN HASHES THAT HAVE MOVED. The grid's route pins 0xDDBC18E9 for the TV
   GUIDE menu and 0x42DBD889 for the empty grid, and both are properties of the broadcast AND of
   how loaded the box is. The menu hash changes when the schedule changes. Seventeen probes go
   through that one route.

WHAT TO DO, in order, because the second is much larger than the first:
  - sweep the probes for t.Fatal/t.Errorf used to report a finding, and convert each to an
    assertion of what was measured;
  - decide what the grid route should pin now. The honest shape is the one openAllChannelsFinished
    uses: pin the screen you SELECT FROM (picture-verified and stable) and let the destination be
    whatever it is, because the destination filling is the thing under test. That is a change to
    what ~17 instruments measure and must be done deliberately, with the artefacts read, not as a
    drive-by.

DO NOT "fix" this by loosening gates. This project has measured the wrong screen five times and
every one was caught by a pin or a picture.

title: Demux.Push ignores the match units, so the model accepts sections the hardware would drop
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-22 while testing whether a PAT reaches the box.

Demux.Push finds the first armed PID channel whose PID matches and writes the section into its ring. IT NEVER CONSULTS THE MATCH UNITS. On real hardware a section is filtered by the unit's byte rules -- table id, extension, and the rest -- before it reaches the firmware; here anything on an armed PID gets through.

THE MODEL IS THEREFORE MORE PERMISSIVE THAN THE HARDWARE, and the consequence is not academic: every experiment that pushes a section on an armed PID can produce a FALSE POSITIVE. 'The box accepted it' where a real box would have dropped it before a single instruction ran. This project has already withdrawn one finding of that family on other grounds -- 'the box keeps our payload, so it accepted' turned out to keep 0xA5, 0x9E, 0xC2 and 0x42 too.

FOUND BY: building a programme association table to ISO 13818-1, pushing it on PID 0x0000 while that channel was open, and having it accepted -- when no match unit on this box filters for table 0x00 at all. The six units carry rules for 0x40, 0x42, 0x4A, 0x73, 0xA3 and 0xC1. A real box would have rejected the PAT outright.

THE FIX is to apply the unit rules in Push, which needs the channel-to-unit mapping the model does not currently represent: there are 32 section channels and 16 match units, and nothing in the code says which unit governs which channel. transport.go:61 uses matchWords[channel][8]&(1<<channel), implying the two are indexed together for the transport path, but that only holds for channels under 16 and the armed channels observed here are 19..24. Establish the mapping from the guest's own register writes before implementing anything.

RISK OF FIXING IT: sections that currently reach the box would stop doing so, which could break acquisition. That is the point -- if our line-up only arrives because the model is too permissive, we do not have a faithful signal path -- but it must be measured, not assumed, and the boot gate and links gate are the checks.

WHY P1: it undermines the evidence value of every push-a-section experiment, which is the main instrument this project uses to find out what the box wants.

title: Send a real transport stream: PAT, PMT and a test-pattern service, so the box stops saying there is no satellite signal
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-22. The box draws 'No satellite signal is being received' and on its own terms it is RIGHT. That string is not a special case: it is one entry in a message table at FLASH 0xAC93F whose neighbours are 'There is a technical fault with this channel' and 'Please try later' -- CHANNEL-level errors, what the box says when it cannot present the service it is tuned to.

THIS PORT GIVES IT NO WAY TO PRESENT ONE, and every part of that is measured:
- demod.Model.Locked() is DEAD CODE. Nothing in the tree calls it, so the fixed 'the front end stays locked' is never communicated to the guest.
- The demux exposes NO sync or lock status -- only filter-completion bits and enables. There is no register on which 'a stream is arriving' could be read.
- The demodulator answers ZERO to every register the box actually reads. The model holds measured values at 11, 34, 74, 75, 78, 92; the cold boot reads 0,1,2,3,4,5,14,1025, all of which fall to the default.
- There is NO TRANSPORT STREAM. Sections are pushed straight into the demux at the section layer. The 188-byte packet path Demux.PushTransport EXISTS, is tested, and NOTHING IN THE PRODUCT USES IT. No PAT, no PMT, no PES, no video.

THE WORK, in the order the box can verify it:
1. PAT on PID 0x0000 and a PMT per service. Both are fully specified in ISO 13818-1, so this does NOT fall foul of phase 7's do-not-guess-a-format rule -- unlike the object carousel, which must be let to name itself. The PMT is what tells the box which PIDs carry a service's video and audio, and until it exists the box cannot ask for them.
2. Feed through Demux.PushTransport as 188-byte packets rather than pushing sections, so the path the hardware actually uses is the path we exercise.
3. A TEST PATTERN as the elementary stream, per the owner's standing decision (gort-0ly): colour bars rather than real MPEG-2 decode.
4. Then re-measure the banner and the ALL CHANNELS grid.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. That the missing signal is WHY the grid draws no rows is a THEORY, not a measurement. The now-and-next banner shows real programmes on the same box at the same time with the same message on screen, so 'no signal' plainly does not stop listings being drawn everywhere. The way to settle it is to send the stream and look -- which is this task.

CHECK FIRST, CHEAPLY: whether the box arms PID 0x0000 at all. The armed set after acquisition is 0x10, 0x11, 0x14, 0x33, 0x34, 0x52 and does NOT include PID 0. A box that never asks for a PAT may need something else first, and a PAT nobody filters for is dropped by the hardware before any code sees it.
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-22, BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS BUILT. Step 1 as written -- 'PAT on PID 0x0000 and a PMT per service' -- does not survive contact with the box.

THE CHEAP CHECK THIS TASK ASKED FOR WAS RUN, and it first looked like good news: PID 0x0000 IS armed, transiently, during acquisition. A single sample misses it; a continuous watch across a session finds it, the same shape as 0x52. So a PAT was built to ISO 13818-1, checked field by field against the specification, and pushed on PID 0 at the moment the channel was open. The model accepted it.

THE BOX DID NOTHING WITH IT. No new PID armed -- in particular not the programme map PID the table named, a number the firmware had no other reason to hold and whose appearance would have proved the table was read and believed. The only PID to appear afterwards was 0x0052, which the record already has opening in response to our NIT.

AND THE HARDWARE WOULD HAVE REJECTED IT. At the moment PID 0 is open, six channels are armed and six match units carry rules -- 0x40/FE (NIT), 0x42/FB (SDT), 0x4A (BAT), 0x73 (TOT), 0xA3 (titles), 0xC1 (A-Z index). NOT ONE FILTERS FOR TABLE 0x00. An open PID channel is not the box asking for a PAT; the channel exists and every rule on this box is looking for something else. It reaches its services without a programme association table, which for an OpenTV Sky receiver driven by NIT, SDT and BAT is entirely reasonable.

SO PAT AND PMT ARE NOT THE WAY IN TO VIDEO, and this task must be re-scoped before it is worked. What replaces it is not yet known and should NOT be guessed: the honest next question is how this firmware learns which PID carries a service's video at all -- most likely from the BAT lineup or a service descriptor it already receives, which would mean the information is already in our broadcast and the gap is elsewhere.

THE EXPERIMENT ONLY REACHED THE BOX BECAUSE OF A MODELLING DEFECT, now gort-85y: Demux.Push delivers to any armed PID WITHOUT applying the match-unit rules, so the model is more permissive than the hardware. That defect blocks this task too -- until it is fixed, 'we sent it and the box accepted it' is not evidence about a real box.

INSTRUMENTS, both committed: internal/multiplex/firmwaretests/everyarmed_firmware_test.go (every PID armed across a whole session, with the phase each first appeared in) and pat_firmware_test.go (send the PAT, dump the channels and units, watch what is armed next). broadcast.PAT exists and is spec-checked in internal/broadcast/pat_test.go -- keep it, it is correct and will be wanted if the route is ever found.
AND THE PID-0 CLAIM ITSELF WAS OUR BUG, fixed 2026-09-22. This is a cleaner reason for the same conclusion.

'PID 0x0000 is armed' came from this port's own ArmedPIDs, which read a channel register, masked the low thirteen bits and reported the result as a PID. A CHANNEL REGISTER OF ZERO IS A CLEARED CHANNEL, NOT A CHANNEL WATCHING PID 0 -- and 0 is a legal PID, so that code could not tell them apart. Looking at the whole word instead of the bottom of it settles it:

    channel 19 -> 00014034    channel 22 -> 00014014
    channel 20 -> 00014033    channel 23 -> 00014011
    channel 24 -> 00014010    the one that read as PID 0 -> 00000000

Every channel the guest programs carries 0x14000 above the PID field; the one that read as PID 0 carries nothing. demux.channelPID now requires those upper bits. The armed set is 0x10, 0x11, 0x14, 0x33, 0x34, 0x52 and PID 0 NEVER APPEARS in any phase of a session.

So there are now TWO independent readings saying the box never asks for a PAT -- the channel registers and the match units, neither of which mentions PID 0 or table 0x00. The earlier conclusion stands and its reason is simpler than the one recorded: not 'the hardware would have rejected it' but 'the box never opened the door at all'.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: gort-85y is still real and still blocks this task. Demux.Push ignoring the match units is what let the PAT reach the guest's ring even though nothing was filtering for it, and it remains true that 'we sent it and the box accepted it' is not evidence about a real box.

GATES after the accessor fix: links gate green (42-task boot, 12 card ISR hits, key dispatcher +27, input events +2, oracle surfaces 9825B318/12 -> F3634409/37). demux, multiplex and broadcast packages green. Lint 0.

title: Decide what the modelled viewing card answers, with evidence
description:
THE WEDGE (gort-slq) IS CAUSED BY THIS PORT'S CARD NOT ANSWERING, measured 2026-09-22: with the card answering only 0x52 and 0x18 the event pipe EVQP0002 fills after 8 handset presses and the box wedges; with every command answered it never fills in 60 presses. The box is not mishandling its own event queue, it is being starved by a peripheral that does not answer.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN IS WHAT A REAL CARD ANSWERS. AckAll replies to every code with a stock frame and that is NOT a viewing card -- a real one answers some commands and refuses others, and answering a refusal as an acceptance will produce a box that is plausibly wrong rather than visibly broken, which is this project's characteristic failure. So the diagnostic must not be shipped as the fix.

THE EVIDENCE TO GATHER, in the shape the record already used for 0x52:
- The opening sequence in docs/reference/digibox-emulation.md lists the codes the box sends: 0x11 0x53 0x54 0x41 0x43 0x42 0x17 unanswered, plus 0x52 and the periodic 0x18 heartbeat. Each needs a decision with a reason.
- 0x52's handler at 0x8002A534 was read off the firmware: it takes frame[3], masks to three bits, stores it and releases Periph unconditionally. The same treatment -- find and read each code's handler -- says what a reply has to contain for the box to accept it, and whether a refusal has a distinct encoding.
- The record's warning applies: 'the box moved on' is NOT evidence a reply was accepted, because advancement is driven by SMTTask's 50-tick timeout. The honest success signal is a frame after the 0x52 that is not the 0x18 heartbeat, or the semaphore's waiter count.

ACCEPTANCE: the ack policy is set from measured handler behaviour rather than from AckAll, the wedge does not reproduce with it, and internal/multiplex/firmwaretests/cardsilence_firmware_test.go still shows its control arm filling when the policy is narrowed back.

Blocks reading any screen that needs more than a few presses to reach, which currently includes A-Z LISTINGS and the ALL CHANNELS grid.
notes:
ANSWERED, 2026-09-22. The policy is {0x52, 0x18, 0x41, 0x42} and it is set from measurement, not preference.

WHICH CODES ARE IN PLAY IS NOT A MATTER OF OPINION. Across the eight presses that fill the pipe the box sends exactly three, taken off the bus (writes to the CSI data register, de-framed with the length field checked against the payload):

    code 18  x3   the heartbeat, already answered
    code 41  x6   SILENT
    code 42  x6   SILENT

0x11, 0x53, 0x54, 0x43, 0x51, 0x10 and 0x22 appear in the boot capture and are NEVER SENT AGAIN while the box fails, so answering them would be a change with no evidence behind it. That disposes of most of the list this bead was filed with.

SWEPT ONE AT A TIME, because two changes at once cannot say which mattered:

    0x52 and 0x18 only       pipe FULL after  8 presses
    and 0x41                 pipe FULL after 10 presses
    and 0x42                 pipe FULL after 10 presses
    and both                 never full in 60, never more than 4 of its 20 messages deep
    every code at all        identical to 'and both'

Either alone barely moves it; together they recover the ENTIRE effect of AckAll. So the policy stops there: what the box demonstrably asks for while it fails, and nothing more. A reply the box accepts where a real card would refuse makes a machine that is plausibly wrong rather than visibly broken, and widening past the evidence is exactly that risk.

THE SNAPSHOT WOULD HAVE EATEN THE FIX, and this is the part worth remembering. Link.Restore put the ack policy back from the blob, and the PRODUCT RESTORES A SNAPSHOT ON EVERY START (cmd/goretrotv/main.go startBox). The two new codes would have worked in every test that boots cold and done nothing at all on the demo, whose post-acquisition.snapshot was written when the policy was two codes long. Green everywhere it is measured, absent where it matters.

Fixed by making the policy MODEL CONFIGURATION rather than machine state -- it says what the peripheral answers, the way the baud rate says how fast -- so Restore takes it from the build. Blob format v4 drops it; v3 blobs are still accepted and their four words consumed and discarded, so existing private snapshots keep loading. The device-contract check (bustest, ARCH-SNAP-1) refused this at first and was RIGHT to: the honest way to say a field is not state is to list it as Constant in the contract, not to quietly drop it from the blob while still claiming completeness.

OUTCOME on the same route that used to stop at three presses: the highlight moves on 18 of 40 (a press landing during a repaint is swallowed, which is ordinary and separately tracked), box office still redraws at the end, and NOTHING EVER SUSPENDS on the queue -- deepest 4 of 20. And A-Z LISTINGS OPENS, nine moves down the TV GUIDE menu, for the first time in this port's life. It draws its header and no rows, which is the same shape as the ALL CHANNELS grid and is now a question that can be asked rather than one blocked behind the wedge.

ACCEPTANCE, all three met: the policy comes from measured behaviour; wedge_firmware_test.go no longer reproduces the wedge and is now a GUARD ON THE CAUSE (the queue's own counters, which catch the failure even on a run where the screen keeps up); and cardsilence_firmware_test.go still shows its control arm filling after 8 presses when the policy is narrowed back.

A SIDE FINDING WITH ITS OWN LESSON: the A-Z probe had been navigating EIGHT entries by the arithmetic that entry 1 plus eight moves is entry 9. Its screenshot says SPECIALIST, which is entry 8. It had been reporting 'A-Z LISTINGS did not read the array' about a screen that was not A-Z LISTINGS, and passing while it did. No amount of read-counting would have caught it -- the instrument was working perfectly and pointed at the wrong thing. What caught it was LOOKING AT THE PICTURE the test had been writing all along.
TWO THINGS THE FIX EXPOSED, and the gates caught both. 2026-09-22.

1. A FRAME-SPLICE DEFECT IN THIS PORT'S OWN LINK, present all along. csi.Link.Pump took the card's reply queue first UNCONDITIONALLY, so a reply generated while a handset frame was part-way out cut straight into it:

    the handset frame      05 80 02 1b 00 07 d0 00
    what the guest got     05 80 02 1b 00 07 | 02 01 41 00 | d0 00 00

Both travel on one wire and share its framing -- bytes until a zero terminator -- so an interrupted frame is not a delayed frame, it is TWO CORRUPT ONES, and the guest's de-framer cannot tell. Invisible for as long as the card answered almost nothing and therefore almost never had anything to say at the wrong moment; widening the policy made it common, and the LINKS GATE caught a cold-boot Sky key that no longer reached the guest's input-event routine (after-key=0 at 0x8006EA04, surface stuck at the baseline 9825B318/12 instead of F3634409/37) while every restored-box test was greener than ever. Fixed: the link finishes the frame it started before changing source. Proved byte for byte by TestACardReplyDoesNotSpliceItselfIntoAHandsetFrame, which failed first.

NOTE ON WRITING THAT TEST: the first version used the command frame 03 01 41 00 and PASSED while proving nothing -- a zero byte IS the terminator on this wire unless escaped, so the frame ended a byte early, failed its own length check and was dropped. 03 06 41 08 out of the record's boot capture is a real one.

2. THE ORACLE DIVERGES, AND THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER. Even with the splice fixed, the cold-boot checkpoint comparison breaks at window 20142 after 20,142 agreeing checkpoints. Both halves measured separately rather than assumed: whole change reverted -> all 470,000 agree; splice fix alone with the old policy -> all 470,000 agree; policy widened -> diverges at twenty million. So it is the ack policy and nothing else.

The browser oracle's card is silent on those codes too, so it would wedge the same way for the same reason. That is the case CLAUDE.md names: the oracle proves this port matches the browser emulator, not that either matches a Digibox; where both are wrong in the same way they agree; inherited errors are caught only by the measured record. This is an inherited error, caught and corrected.

RESOLUTION: the oracle file is UNTOUCHED -- editing it to agree is the one move that destroys its value. The comparison instead runs in the oracle's declared condition, via a new -ack-oracle flag holding the card to {0x52,0x18}, exactly as it already runs WITHOUT -sky-gates against a stream named oracle-cold-boot-nogates. The product ships the fix; the comparison runs the oracle's card; both facts are stated wherever either is relied on. Recorded as an architecture decision in plan/module-decisions.md with its rejected alternatives, and summarised in CLAUDE.md.

GATES: oracle-gate AGREE over 470,000 checkpoints; links-gate green with oracle surfaces 9825B318/12 -> F3634409/37 and the key reaching both the dispatcher (+27) and the input-event routine (+2).
close_reason:
ANSWERED AND SHIPPED in 9919681. csi.DefaultAckPolicy = {0x52, 0x18, 0x41, 0x42}, set from measurement.

The box sends exactly three codes across the eight presses that fill EVQP0002 -- 0x18 x3, 0x41 x6, 0x42 x6 -- taken off the bus and de-framed with the length field checked. Swept one at a time: control FULL after 8 presses, +0x41 after 10, +0x42 after 10, +both never in 20, every code identical to both. Either alone barely moves it; together they recover the entire effect of AckAll, so the policy stops there rather than widening to codes the box never asks for while it fails.

ACCEPTANCE, all three met:
- the policy comes from measured handler behaviour rather than AckAll;
- wedge_firmware_test.go no longer reproduces the wedge and is now a GUARD ON THE CAUSE -- it watches the queue's own counters, so it catches the failure even on a run where the screen keeps up (12 of 20 presses move, 7 of 20 messages deep, 0 tasks ever suspended);
- cardcodes_firmware_test.go pins the pre-fix policy and still shows the queue filling after 8 presses when it is narrowed back.

THE FIX EXPOSED TWO THINGS AND FIXED BOTH. A frame splice in this port's own link, present all along and invisible while the card had nothing to say: replies took priority unconditionally, so one generated mid-frame cut into a handset frame. The links gate caught it as a cold-boot Sky key that no longer reached the input-event routine while every restored-box test was greener than ever. And a loose guide-subscription instrument that stopped at a slot which EXISTED rather than one that had been filled in.

THE ORACLE DIVERGES BY DESIGN, controlled both ways: fully reverted, all 470,000 checkpoints agree; splice fix alone, all 470,000 agree; policy widened, diverges at twenty million. The oracle's card is silent on the same codes and would wedge identically -- an inherited error. The oracle is untouched; the comparison runs -ack-oracle in its declared condition, as it already runs without -sky-gates. Recorded in plan/module-decisions.md with rejected alternatives and summarised in CLAUDE.md.

GATES: oracle 470,000 checkpoints AGREE; links green (9825B318/12 -> F3634409/37, key reaching dispatcher +27 and input events +2); replay, snapshot, cpu, handoff green; conformance 7/7; lint 0; full race suite green.

STILL OPEN, and stated rather than implied: whether a real card answers 0x41 and 0x42 with a bare acknowledgement. A differential PC census was tried and does not work -- past the first divergence the two arms' schedules differ and the diff is a schedule, not a handler. The instrument that would settle it is a watch on the assembled reply frame in RAM naming every PC that reads it, and it is worth building when the answer becomes load-bearing.

title: Drive the box only through its modelled inputs, retiring each host poke
description:
WHAT IT IS, in the owner's words (2026-09-21):
"we should pursue the satellite signal route, just use a test image for video/audio" and, on being
shown the line-up measurement task: "if that's the old inject flash/memory shit, weren't we dropping
that for REAL satellite signal work so we can inject it at the signal source and run menu,
video/audio and everything else".

The direction: STOP SATISFYING THE BOX BY POKING IT, and satisfy it from the transponder instead --
so the menu, the carousel, logos, menu audio and the guide all come up because the box got what it
was asking for, not because the host answered on its behalf. Video and audio stand in as a TEST
IMAGE / test pattern rather than real MPEG-2 decode.

WHY IT IS CREDIBLE, and this is the part that turns it from a preference into a hypothesis:
internal/machine/sky_gates.go is a HOST INTERVENTION that makes the Sky menu appear at all. After
42 guest tasks exist it patches FLASH BYTE 0x72FA1 from 0x75 to 0x76 and writes 0 over RAM WORD
0x80054F84 (previously 0xFFFFFFFF). Nobody knows what either gate is ASKING. It is inherited from
the browser oracle as a "declared presentation policy", and CLAUDE.md's own warning covers exactly
this case: the oracle proves this port matches the browser emulator, not that either matches a
Digibox, and where both are wrong in the same way they agree.

So the box has been TOLD to draw the menu rather than satisfied that it should. That is a plausible
single cause for several symptoms currently tracked as separate puzzles: the object carousel never
asks (gort-qxl.4), 0x800BECF0 has never executed once, PID 0x52 is armed and unfed (gort-qxl.3),
ALL CHANNELS draws no rows (gort-qxl.1), and the box reports "No satellite signal is being received"
while performing ZERO demodulator reads.

WHICH RECORDED DECISIONS IT RE-OPENS -- it is a re-litigation and must be treated as one:
1. CLAUDE.md "The Sky menu gates are a separate declared presentation policy... Report this host
   intervention explicitly; keep clean hardware oracle runs free of it." Replacing the gates with
   real stimulus changes a recorded architecture decision.
2. CLAUDE.md Out of Scope (v1): "MPEG-2 video and the video plane (phase: Video)". A test image on
   the video plane re-opens that, even though a test pattern is far cheaper than a decoder. There is
   NO video plane today: board.Compose() delegates to Display.Compose() (the OSD only), and
   internal/device/osd/video.go is an MMIO register model, not a renderer.
3. The oracle contract. The oracle runs WITH the declared policy; a port that no longer needs it may
   diverge from the oracle at the gate, and the oracle is the only independent check this port has.
   How the oracle comparison survives is an open question, not a detail.

THE COST AND RISK THAT MUST BE ANSWERED:
- The Sky/OpenTV carousel format is NOT publicly documented. Research confirms the generic DSM-CC
  shape (DSI -> DII -> DDB, moduleId/moduleVersion/carouselType) is well specified, but no public
  source describes what THIS firmware expects. Phase 7's own rule applies and is written in blood:
  DO NOT GUESS A FORMAT -- four section formats were built, fed and measured, and a guessed fifth is
  how a day gets wasted. The box must name what it wants.
- Identifying what the two gates ask is reverse engineering of unknown size. It may be one
  entitlement word and it may be a chain.
- "No satellite signal is being received" is drawn with ZERO demodulator reads, so it is NOT taken
  off the front end. Richer RF/demod modelling will not clear it, and anyone who assumes otherwise
  will spend a day on the wrong layer.

WHAT A SPEC WOULD HAVE TO SETTLE -- the actual open questions:
Q1. What does RAM 0x80054F84 mean to the application, and what writes it in a real box? Same for
    flash 0x72FA1 -- is it NVRAM-backed state, an entitlement, a service record, a carousel flag?
Q2. Can either gate be satisfied by broadcast alone, or does one require NVRAM/smartcard state?
    If a gate genuinely requires a card, "signal only" is not achievable and the policy stays.
Q3. Does the box composite a video plane at all, and what does it expect to be there? A test image
    needs a plane, a format and a path into Compose().
Q4. What does the oracle comparison become if the port no longer needs the declared policy? Does the
    gate stay behind a flag for oracle runs?
Q5. Is menu audio driven by the firmware at all (already TASK-7.6, a measurement -- "no" is an
    acceptable answer and would close a third of this idea).
Q6. Does the twelve-versus-six line-up discrepancy dissolve once the gates are answered properly?

WHERE IT WOULD LAND: mostly phase 7 (gort-qxl), which already owns the carousel, PID 0x52, the
DSM-CC format and the audio measurement. The video test image does NOT fit phase 7 and would need a
new phase, since it re-opens a v1 scope decision.

NEXT STEP: /architect the gates-and-signal question (Q1, Q2, Q4 first -- they decide whether the
rest is even reachable), then /spike Q1 against the real firmware, then come back through
/feature-intake promote. NOTHING IS BUILT until then.
notes:
THE PRINCIPLE, stated by the owner 2026-09-21 and adopted as the frame for this idea:
"Poking memory feels wrong when we should be emulating the hardware and what goes into the hardware
inputs (sat signal, RF, buttons etc)."

This is an ARCHITECTURAL STANCE, not a preference, and it is worth recording as one. A hardware
model earns its correctness by being driven only through the inputs the real device has. Every host
poke is a claim the model could not support -- and, worse, it is a claim that HIDES the thing it
substitutes for, because the symptom it was covering never surfaces again.

THE BOX'S REAL INPUTS, all four already modelled as devices:
  satellite front end   internal/device/demod (I2C tuner/demodulator) + internal/device/demux
                        (PID filters, match units) -> the transport stream
  viewing card          internal/device/smartcard -- and note WHAT it models: port.go says "the
                        framed controller behind the second card slot". It is a UART: frames, paced
                        reply bytes, status registers. It is the TRANSPORT, not a card that answers
                        entitlement questions.
  handset               internal/device/csi (the clock synchronous serial link)
  modem                 internal/device/modem (return path, unused in v1)

THE HOST INTERVENTIONS THIS PRINCIPLE INDICTS -- there are TWO, not one:
1. APPLICATION ENTRY. CLAUDE.md: "The host changes PC/ISA/RA once after the bootloader is idle and
   the flash header checks; guest code then decompresses and runs the application." The bootloader
   does not hand off on its own. Something about the boot is unmodelled and this covers it.
2. THE SKY MENU GATES (internal/machine/sky_gates.go). After 42 guest tasks: flash byte 0x72FA1
   0x75 -> 0x76, and RAM word 0x80054F84 0xFFFFFFFF -> 0.

AND THE RECORD ALREADY NAMES A CANDIDATE FOR WHAT THEY ARE COVERING. From
docs/reference/digibox-emulation.md, "The smartcard link -- why the box stops": "The application
boots, creates all six of its tasks, and then every one of them blocks. The thing it is waiting for
is the viewing card. This is the gate; nothing downstream of it -- video, the OSD, the EPG -- can be
reached until the card answers."

So the hypothesis this idea should test FIRST, because it is one question that could explain both
interventions and several open phase-7 puzzles: ARE THE HOST POKES SUBSTITUTING FOR A VIEWING CARD
THAT NEVER PROPERLY ANSWERS? We model the card's UART; we may not model a card. If the real gate is
entitlement state that a card would supply, then no amount of richer BROADCAST will clear it -- and
that would be a genuinely important finding, because it means "the satellite signal route" is the
right principle applied to the wrong input.

REFRAMED GOAL, sharper than "emulate the satellite signal": DRIVE THE BOX ONLY THROUGH ITS MODELLED
INPUTS, AND RETIRE EACH HOST INTERVENTION BY FINDING THE INPUT THAT SHOULD HAVE SATISFIED IT. Each
retirement is independently verifiable -- the intervention is deleted and the box still reaches the
same screen -- which is a far better acceptance test than "the menu looks right".

ADDS TO THE OPEN QUESTIONS:
Q7. Does a viewing card answer today, and what does the firmware ask it? Is the smartcard model a
    port with no card behind it?
Q8. Can application entry (intervention 1) be retired too, or is the bootloader genuinely waiting on
    something unmodelled? Retiring it is a much larger claim than retiring the menu gates.
Q9. What is the ACCEPTANCE TEST for a retired intervention -- presumably: delete it, boot, and reach
    the same measured state hash. That is checkable and should be written before any of this starts.
CONSTRAINT, owner, 2026-09-21: 'no more memory poking (it's fine to debug and read/write memory to see what works and decompile using ghidra etc and any other tool)'.

The line is between the PRODUCT and the INSTRUMENTS, and it is not 'never touch memory':
  FORBIDDEN -- the shipped emulator depending on a host write to function. sky_gates.go patching
    flash 0x72FA1 and RAM 0x80054F84 to make the menu appear is the case in point. A model that
    needs a poke to reach a screen has not modelled the thing that screen depends on.
  PERMITTED, and encouraged -- reading and WRITING memory in instruments, tests and spikes to find
    out what works: read-watches, write-watches, probes, forcing a value to test a hypothesis,
    bisecting a gate by hand. A debugger that cannot write is half a debugger.
  PERMITTED -- Ghidra and any other static tool on the firmware images for decompilation. That is
    how the o-code parser, the 0xB1 entry layout and the demux match units were read in the first
    place.

So the test for any proposed change is: IF THE INSTRUMENTS WERE ALL REMOVED, WOULD THE BOX STILL
REACH THIS SCREEN? If the answer needs a host write, it is not finished.

Note the existing gdb stub (internal/gdbstub) is on the permitted side and is already localhost-only
by ARCH-DEV-1 -- it is a debugger, not a mechanism the product depends on.

title: The box wedges: three tasks pile onto pipe EVQP0002 and the event task stops running
description:
Measured 2026-09-21 while sampling the ALL CHANNELS grid on the live demo at 47e1f01.

Three scripted trials pressed the identical sequence on the identical cadence: back-up, back-up, box office (7s settle), LEFT (7s), select (16s). Trials 1 and 3 drove the box normally -- the canvas hash moved through the sky menu (ink 22428), the filled TV GUIDE tab (35700) and the grid (3161). TRIAL 2 PRODUCED NO CANVAS CHANGE AT ALL across its full ~38 seconds: every press was ignored and the screen stayed on the frame it was already showing.

Not diagnosed. Candidates, none eliminated: the 64-message key queue in internal/web/transport.go; the box not being in phase ready so keys are refused at transport.go:261-266; the known 'a key is lost if pressed while the menu is still painting' behaviour (recorded for 0x5C in docs/reference/digibox-emulation.md) generalising to other keys; or another viewer on the shared box changing state underneath the run.

WHY IT MATTERS: it is a strong candidate for the owner-reported 'sometimes it stays blank' on the TV guide, and it is NOT a listings fault -- if presses are dropped you never leave the screen you are on. It also silently invalidates any measurement that assumes a key landed, which is this project's oldest failure mode.

FIRST STEP: reproduce with the page's own key-feedback text captured alongside the canvas hash -- app.ts sets '<key> sent to the box.' on a successful send and 'The box is not ready for handset input.' when it refuses. That one string separates 'the browser never sent it' from 'the box ignored it' and costs nothing.
notes:
DIAGNOSED 2026-09-21 on a LOCAL box (no other viewers, debug logging, post-acquisition snapshot,
live clock, real listings). The effect is real and reproduces. My original framing over-claimed and
is corrected below.

TRANSPORT IS EXONERATED -- this is not a dropped message.
37 key presses, every one logged server-side as "handset key queued on CSI" with its raw code and
retired count. ZERO "key queue full", ZERO "box is not ready", ZERO closes, ZERO halts. The browser
reported "<key> sent to the box." each time. Across twelve presses the retired count climbed
1,335,362,560 -> 1,829,614,592, so the box was executing throughout, not wedged. Every candidate in
the original description -- the 64-message queue, the ready-phase refusal at transport.go:261-266,
the client not sending -- is eliminated by measurement.

THE EFFECT, REPRODUCED. Three identical trials, same cadence, same keys:

    trial 1   select -> the grid      85c9173a -> 85c9173a   NO CHANGE   (0x5C swallowed)
    trial 2   box office FROM GRID    5c152d74 -> 5c152d74   NO CHANGE   (0x7D swallowed)
    trial 3   box office FROM GRID    5c152d74 -> d747c730   MOVED

Same key, same screen, same settle: absorbed in trial 2, honoured in trial 3. The key reached the
CSI in BOTH cases. So the firmware receives the press and produces no screen change.

THIS IS THE RECORDED 0x5C BEHAVIOUR, WIDER THAN RECORDED. docs/reference/digibox-emulation.md
already notes that 0x5C "is lost if it is pressed while the menu is still painting" and treats it as
a measurement-technique caveat. It is not confined to select: 0x7D shows it too, and it is not only
a measurement problem -- it is what a viewer experiences as "I pressed it and nothing happened".

CORRECTION TO MY ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION. "Ignores every handset press for tens of seconds" is wrong.
What the earlier live-demo trial 2 actually showed was a sequence in which the FIRST key was
swallowed and the rest were no-ops for ordinary reasons, which I read as a total freeze. Specifically
I conflated "no change expected" with "ignored": pressing box office while already on the box office
tab correctly redraws the same frame, and back up appears to do nothing on these screens at all
(0/5 presses moved the screen) -- though the record shows the firmware runs 3706 o-code fetches over
946 idle-never-visited addresses on 0x3C, so it IS received and processed. Whether back up SHOULD
change these screens is not established here and needs a reference, not a guess.

WHAT A VIEWER CAN RELY ON, measured:
  tv guide (0x80) escaped the grid in both trials that reached it -- the reliable exit.
  up/down (0x58/0x59) moved the menu selection every time.
  back up (0x3C) never changed the screen: 0 of 5.

HYPOTHESIS WORTH TESTING, NOT ASSERTED: the swallow window may be an artefact of our speed. The box
retires ~3.2M instr/s against the 15M/s NFR (gort-4sx.29), so every repaint lasts roughly five times
longer here than on real hardware and the window in which a key is absorbed is proportionally wider.
If so this would be a rare annoyance on a real Digibox and a frequent one on the demo, and closing
gort-4sx.29 would shrink it without any input-path change. TEST: measure the swallow RATE (presses
absorbed per hundred, on a fixed screen and cadence) before and after any instructions-per-second
work. Do not "fix" the input path until that is known -- queueing or retrying a key the firmware
deliberately dropped would diverge from the hardware, which is the one thing this port must not do.

NEXT: instrument where the press dies inside the firmware. The event loop is 0x9FC4A538 and the key
handler 0x9FC4A6A0 (record, "the key reaches the application's real handler"). Compare a swallowed
press with an honoured one at that handler: if both reach 0x9FC4A6A0 the loss is above it in the
o-code, and if only one does the loss is in the native dispatcher.
THIS IS A WEDGE, NOT AN ABSORBED PRESS. 2026-09-22, and it upgrades this issue to P1.

Measured while chasing gort-ybj: after a few TV GUIDE menu presses the box stops responding to input ENTIRELY. Not the key, not the menu -- UP dies, DOWN dies, and box office, which leaves the menu altogether, dies too. The stop point VARIES between runs (five moves, then three), which a disabled menu entry would not do.

THE RTOS NAMES IT. At the wall [0x801072B0] -- Nucleus TCD_Execute_Task, this project's own 'single cheapest health check on the whole system' -- reads ZERO, and so does [0x801072D8]. Every task is blocked and the guest sits in the idle loop at 0x800D35DC. It is NOT halted: it retired two million further instructions while unresponsive.

Task census at the wall (only status 7 is established by the record as an event wait; 5 and 6 are printed raw rather than named, because naming them would put a guess where a reader takes a reading):
    TASK0    status=7 runs=1883     EVENT WAIT
    TASK1    status=7 runs=75       EVENT WAIT
    SMNTask  status=7 runs=10430    EVENT WAIT
    SMHKTask status=5 runs=5
    SMTTask  status=5 runs=2189
    EVTTask  status=5 runs=49124
    FETask   status=6 runs=11978
    SCTask   status=6 runs=1

WHY P1 NOW: this description -- 'a key press is intermittently absorbed' -- understates it. The box does not drop a press, it stops running anything, and it does not recover. Every measurement taken after several menu presses is suspect until this is understood, which includes any future attempt to open a screen by navigating to it. gort-ybj ('the menu will not pass entry 6') was filed on this behaviour and is withdrawn as a symptom of it.

INSTRUMENT: internal/multiplex/firmwaretests/menustop_firmware_test.go reproduces it in about fourteen seconds and prints the RTOS state and the task census. It REPORTS rather than fails, because failing on a tracked defect would red the suite; when this is fixed that log becomes the assertion.

NEXT: three tasks are in EVENT WAIT and three on semaphores. The record reached its smartcard conclusion by reading the waiting task's stack for the return address -- 'its stack carries a return into 0x8002A44F, inside the smartcard driver'. Do that here for TASK0 and SMNTask and the thing the box is waiting for gets a name.
NARROWED TO THREE TASKS OF FORTY-TWO, 2026-09-22 -- and two of them are the smartcard module.

THE EARLIER NOTE ON THIS BEAD OVERSTATED ITS EVIDENCE. It reported 'every task is blocked' as the finding. A control taken BEFORE any key is pressed says otherwise: an idle box has every task blocked too. Each of the 42 tasks waits on its own private EVENT00 event group or on its subsystem's command queue -- TASK6 on QUEU BlitReq, TASK7 on QUEU dmxmsgQ, FETask on SEMA FeCmd, SCTask on SEMA SCSV0, ECM on QUEU ECM -- which is what idle looks like on this firmware. The earlier census also listed eight tasks because it only asked about eight names it already knew; there are 42.

SO THE READING IS THE DIFF, AND IT IS THREE LINES:

    SMTTask   status=7 EVNT SMTEvts  ->  status=5, nothing names it
    SMHKTask  status=7 EVNT SHKEvts  ->  status=5, nothing names it
    EVTTask   status=6 SEMA EVTTick  ->  status=5 SEMA EVQS0002 + PIPE EVQP0002

(A fourth line, TASK15 status=0 -> 7, is the sample instant: it held the CPU when the control was taken. The instrument labels it.)

SMTTask is the smartcard TRANSMIT task and SMHKTask its housekeeping task -- the one whose periodic 0x18 heartbeat the record describes as having 'no retry counter and nothing that will ever stop it'. Both leave their event groups for a state where NO kernel object names them, which is not what a semaphore or event-group wait looks like. EVTTask is the EVENT task: a handset press must become an event before any screen sees it, and the task that delivers events has moved off its tick onto the event queue pair.

WHICH WAY THE CAUSATION RUNS IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The smartcard module stalling and the event task stalling are each consistent with the other going first. Naming a culprit here would be a guess. What is established is where to look, and it is not the menu.

INSTRUMENT: internal/multiplex/firmwaretests/wedge_firmware_test.go (renamed from menustop_firmware_test.go). Takes the idle control, walks to the wall in ~20s, prints the diff and the full wait map. Reports rather than fails.

MACHINERY, now part of the port: internal/board/nucleus.go reads the guest's Nucleus control blocks -- Tasks() with TCB addresses, NucleusObjects() (242 found: 138 SEMA, 42 TASK, 31 EVNT, 13 HISR, 11 QUEU, 5 PIPE), TaskWaits() naming what each task is queued on. Read-only, no poking. Three traps it had to get past, all of them plausible wrong answers first: scanning for pointers TO a task finds its stale stack rather than its suspension (it reported TASK0 on six semaphores at once); a four-letter magic plus a printable name is also what ordinary English looks like, so the created-list node in front of the block is what separates them; and the name field carries stale bytes past its terminator (TASK0 reads 54 41 53 4b 30 00 30 00), so insisting on a clean tail drops the very task this is about.

NEXT: read the flash for what SMTEvts and SHKEvts are set by, and whether the 0x18 heartbeat is still going out at the wall. The smartcard link is an INPUT, which puts this on the main line rather than beside it.
EVTTask STOPS BEING SCHEDULED. Measured 2026-09-22, same instrument.

Status is a state and a state can be one a task passes through constantly, so the earlier 'three tasks moved' reading needed the blunter question: which tasks still RUN. Nucleus keeps each task's own schedule count, so two samples either side of one window answer it.

    working, idle (2,000,000 instructions):  EVTTask +89  SMNTask +23  SMTTask +4  TASK2 +2  TASK24 +3  TASK15 +1
    at the wall  (2,000,000 instructions):                SMNTask +6               TASK2 +2  TASK24 +2  FETask +1

EVTTask -- the EVENT task -- runs eighty-nine times while the handset works and NOT ONCE at the wall. SMTTask likewise drops to zero. A handset press has to become an event before any screen sees it, and the task that delivers events has stopped running.

THE HARDWARE UNDERNEATH IS FINE, so this is not an input that died on us. Over the same two windows: board timer accessed 176 times on BOTH sides, identical; interrupt controller 214 vs 188; CPU exception vector entered 116 vs 102. The CSI link the handset arrives on still carries traffic (54 reads / 15 data writes working, 18 / 6 at the wall) and NOTHING IS LEFT QUEUED ON IT -- the key bytes were delivered and consumed. The press reaches the guest, as this bead always said. What fails is downstream of it.

ALL THREE MOVERS END UP ON A PIPE, and EVTTask's is the event pipe:

    SMTTask   status=7 EVNT SMTEvts  ->  status=5 (a pipe wait)
    SMHKTask  status=7 EVNT SHKEvts  ->  status=5 PIPE EVQP0002
    EVTTask   status=6 SEMA EVTTick  ->  status=5 (a pipe wait)

Read that as a producer/consumer stall on EVQP0002: the consumer of the event pipe is never scheduled again. Which way the causation runs -- smartcard module first or event task first -- is NOT established, and asserting it would be a guess.

A SIDE FINDING WORTH ITS OWN LINE: the task status numbers are now measured rather than assumed. Every suspended task is queued on an object whose type is read out of the guest, so the correlation names them -- 4 is a QUEU wait (x10), 6 a SEMA wait (x7), 7 an EVNT wait (x21), each with exactly ONE object type against it across 42 tasks; 5 is a PIPE wait, on one confirmed instance plus two the scan's window still misses; 0 is runnable and 2 is UTIL's timer sleep. The record previously had only 'status 7 means event wait'.

NEXT: find EVQP0002's producer. The pipe is a named object at a known address, so who writes to it is answerable by watching the bus rather than by reading more disassembly.
THE WEDGE HAS A NAME: PIPE EVQP0002, at guest 0x8011B834. 2026-09-22.

All three tasks that move are queued on the SAME pipe:

    SMTTask   status=7 EVNT SMTEvts  ->  status=5 PIPE EVQP0002
    SMHKTask  status=7 EVNT SHKEvts  ->  status=5 PIPE EVQP0002
    EVTTask   status=6 SEMA EVTTick  ->  status=5 PIPE EVQP0002

Three tasks piled on one pipe, one of them that pipe's own consumer, and the consumer never scheduled again (EVTTask: +89 runs per 2M instructions while working, 0 at the wall). Nothing drains it, so nothing can write to it, so no press becomes an event and every screen stops.

NAMING ALL THREE TOOK A FIX TO THE INSTRUMENT, NOT ANOTHER RUN, and the failure mode is worth keeping. Only the FIRST waiter on a Nucleus object is reachable from the object itself; the rest chain off it on the list node. Stopping at the head reported EVTTask as 'status 5, nothing names it' -- a task waiting on something unknown, rather than the third member of a pile-up on one pipe. Those two readings point at entirely different next steps and only one of them is true. TaskWaits now walks the chain, bounded, stopping at the first node that does not name a task.

The status map is also complete now, every suspended status with exactly one object type against it across 42 tasks: 4=QUEU x10, 5=PIPE x3, 6=SEMA x7, 7=EVNT x21, 0 runnable, 2 a timer sleep (UTIL, nothing names it).

WHICH END BLOCKED FIRST IS NOT ESTABLISHED. A producer blocked on a full pipe and a consumer that stopped draining it are each an explanation of the other, and picking one here would be a guess.

NEXT INSTRUMENT: the pipe itself. EVQP0002 is a named object at a known address with EVQS0002 (0x8011B80C) beside it, so who writes to it, how full it is, and at which instruction it stops being drained are bus questions -- a read/write watch on the pipe's control block across the working window and the wall, the same shape as the CSI watch already in wedge_firmware_test.go.
THE PIPE IS FULL AND ABANDONED -- both halves measured, 2026-09-22.

EVQP0002 at guest 0x8011B834, the same two windows side by side:

    while working:  empty, 0 tasks suspended,  read 8011B780 write 8011B780,  53 distinct PCs touched it
    at the wall:    FULL -- not one of its 160 bytes free, holding 20 messages of 8 bytes,
                    3 tasks suspended,         read 8011B7A0 write 8011B7A0,  NOTHING touched it

Fifty-three pieces of code read and write that pipe while the handset works. At the wall, across two million instructions, NOT ONE INSTRUCTION touches it, while three tasks sit queued on it and every byte is spoken for. It is not contended, it is abandoned. That accounts for the whole symptom: no press becomes an event, so the menu will not move and box office will not redraw.

WHICH END STOPPED FIRST IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED. A producer blocked on a full pipe and a consumer that stopped draining it are each an explanation of the other.

NEXT THREAD: the 53 PCs. They are a contiguous run from 0x80034742, the same region EVTTask's suspend block sits in (0x80034CBC). Disassemble it with tools/disasm.sh and the send and receive sides separate.

TWO INSTRUMENT HABITS WORTH KEEPING, both wrong first:
- The dump must be trimmed to the block. Reading 0x40 words past a control block under 0x50 bytes long printed twenty lines of the NEXT structure as though they were the pipe's -- orderly, plausible, unrelated.
- The layout must be checked before it is named, and here the check REFUSED. The obvious reading made +0x30 the end of the buffer; the object census independently names 0x8011B80C as the semaphore EVQS0002 and +0x48 as the event group SMTEvts. This block carries pointers to its SIBLING OBJECTS where the textbook layout carries a buffer bound, so assuming the layout would have measured a length from a semaphore's address and produced a confident number.
- The message size is derived from the EMPTY sample, not looked up: a field reading 0 when the pipe is empty and 20 when full is a count, so messages are 160/20 = 8 bytes and the neighbouring 32 is unidentified. Read the other way round it gives five slots and no account of the other field. Neither changes the finding, because FULL comes from the free count reaching zero.
ONE PRODUCER, ONE CONSUMER, AND THE KEYS REALLY ARE THE CAUSE. 2026-09-22.

THE 53 PCs, DISASSEMBLED (tools/disasm.sh). Three clusters, not one:
    0x800CEBA0  the SEND half     -- adds one to the message count at 0x800CED50, every store to the free-byte field SUBTRACTS
    0x800CED68  the RECEIVE half  -- takes one off at 0x800CEEDE, every store to the free-byte field ADDS
    0x80034734  the application's consumer, calling the receive wrapper and switching on its status
Both halves are reached through checking wrappers (0x800CF1A4 -> send, 0x800CF218 -> receive) which validate the caller against the four-character "PIPE" id at 0x800CF294 -- the same magic the object census finds by scanning DRAM, reached from the other direction.

THE WHOLE CONTROL BLOCK now falls out of those routines: +0x0C id, +0x18 byte 0 = variable-size flag, +0x1C buffer length, +0x20 messages held, +0x24 message size (a MAXIMUM, this pipe being variable-size), +0x28 bytes free, +0x2C/+0x30 buffer start and end, +0x34 read pointer (receive only), +0x38 write pointer (send only), +0x3C tasks suspended, +0x44 suspension list. The pipe is EMBEDDED in a composite: semaphore EVQS0002 at 0x8011B80C, pipe at +0x28 = 0x8011B834, buffer 0x8011B76C..0x8011B80C ending exactly where the composite begins.

WHO, NOT JUST WHAT. Reading TCD_Execute_Task at each access names the task behind every one:
    while working:  EVTTask SENDING to it 16 accesses, SMTTask RECEIVING from it 15
    at the wall:    NOTHING touched it
EVTTask is the ONLY sender and SMTTask the ONLY receiver. At the wall SMTTask -- the sole consumer -- is itself suspended on the SEND side of the same pipe, with EVTTask and SMHKTask behind it. Self-deadlock, measured end to end.

AND THE KEYS ARE THE CAUSE, which was worth checking because it looked like they might not be. 500,000,000 instructions with NOTHING TOUCHED: the count field was written 444 times and the pipe never got deeper than 1 of 20 messages, with 0 tasks ever suspended. So it does not drift into the wall on its own -- a key press costs SMTTask something it cannot absorb.

NEXT: what SMTTask has to do per event. The CSI carries the handset AND the smartcard on one wire, and this port's own link pacing is flagged in the record as ours rather than the firmware's and load-bearing (TrafficInstructions=2100, IdleInstructions=320000, csi.SetAckPolicy answering only 0x52 and 0x18 while the box sends 0x11 0x53 0x54 0x41 0x43 0x42 0x17 unanswered and advances on a 50-tick timeout). If each drained event makes SMTTask send a command and wait out that timeout, twenty events is a handful of presses. Testable by widening the ack policy in a spike and seeing whether the wedge survives.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER NOTES ON THIS BEAD, both plausible when written:
- 'the block carries pointers to its sibling objects' -- NO. +0x30 is the buffer's end and merely coincides with the composite's base, because the buffer runs up to it. Two addresses that coincide are not a pointer.
- 'the 32 is unidentified, messages are 8 bytes' -- both size fields are real: +0x24 is the API-validated MAXIMUM, +0x20 is the count. Messages sent are 4 bytes stored in 8.

INSTRUMENTS: internal/multiplex/firmwaretests/wedge_firmware_test.go (the wall, the pipe, the tasks behind every access) and eventpipe_firmware_test.go (the untouched-box control). The second one FIRST REPORTED THE OPPOSITE by sampling the pipe every 2M instructions and finding it empty every time -- the depth is a transient, and polling a transient is not observing an event. It now watches the writes to the count field.
THE WEDGE IS OURS. The modelled card's silence is what fills the pipe. 2026-09-22.

Both arms acquire identically and differ only in what the front-panel peripheral answers afterwards:

    card answers 0x52 and 0x18 only:   EVQP0002 full after 8 presses    (deepest 20 of 20)
    card answers everything (AckAll):  never full in 60 presses         (deepest  4 of 20)

Eight presses against sixty and counting. The handset and the viewing card share one wire, and the pipe is drained by SMTTask, the smartcard module's transmit task. Our card answers two codes because those are the two the record measured; the box also sends 0x11 0x53 0x54 0x41 0x43 0x42 0x17 and advances past them on SMTTask's fifty-tick timeout. Each drained event costs SMTTask a timeout, so twenty outstanding events is a handful of presses. The box is NOT mishandling its own event queue -- it is being starved by a peripheral that does not answer.

THIS IS A DIAGNOSTIC AND NOT A FIX. AckAll replies to every code with a stock frame, which is not what a viewing card does -- a real one answers some and refuses others. It says WHERE the cause is, not what the card should say. The pipe still reaches 4 of 20 with everything answered, so the pressure is real and merely absorbed.

It is input-side, not a poke: what changes is what the modelled peripheral answers, the same class of thing as the link's baud rate that the record already calls ours and load-bearing. Nothing is written into the guest.

INSTRUMENT: internal/multiplex/firmwaretests/cardsilence_firmware_test.go. The control arm asserts it reproduces the wedge, because an experiment whose control shows no effect has nothing for its other arm to be compared against.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD: decide what the card should actually answer, with evidence. That is gort-h4k.
CORRECTION to the line above: the follow-up bead is gort-b9n, not gort-h4k. That id was written into the note before the bead existed and was never a real one -- an id is a fact about the tracker, not a placeholder to fill in later.
The untouched-box control (eventpipe_firmware_test.go) has been RETIRED, 2026-09-22. Its finding stands and is in the record: 500,000,000 instructions with nothing touched, the message count written 444 times, never deeper than 1 of 20, nobody ever suspended -- so the box does not drift into the wall on its own and the keys were the cause.

The instrument cost a full acquisition plus 300M instructions in a package that runs under -race against a thirty-minute cap it has hit before, and what it guarded against is now covered by wedge_firmware_test.go, which watches the same queue's counters across thirty presses. A finding worth keeping is not the same as an instrument worth keeping.
close_reason:
FIXED by gort-b9n, shipped in 9919681.

The box wedged because EVQP0002 has exactly one consumer, SMTTask, and every key press made the box send two commands the modelled card did not answer -- so SMTTask ate its fifty-tick timeout per event, the queue filled, and the sole consumer ended up suspended trying to add to the very pipe it alone drains. Answering 0x41 and 0x42 removes the starvation.

VERIFIED: the menu now navigates all ten entries, box office still leaves it, and A-Z LISTINGS opens for the first time in this port's life. Across twenty presses the queue reaches 7 of its 20 messages with NOTHING ever suspended on it, against 20 of 20 with three suspended before. wedge_firmware_test.go is now a regression guard on the cause rather than a characterisation, and it diagnoses in full when it trips -- the task census against its idle control, the pipe's counters, and which code and which task last touched it.

The wedge's whole diagnosis is in docs/reference/digibox-emulation.md, including the readings that were withdrawn along the way.

title: Make the non-redistributable dictionary rule true and mechanised
description:
The Sky Huffman dictionary is asserted to be "never committed and never baked into a published image" in four places (.gitignore:35-39, dictionaries/MANIFEST.md, docker-compose.yml:33-34, internal/broadcast/huffman.go:18-20). The assertion is FALSE and has been since the first commit.

Two byte-identical copies are tracked at HEAD and on the PUBLIC origin/master:
  tools/skyepg/skyuk.dict
  web/data/skyuk.dict
Both sha256 c05d288d9d22403f97e5caade329579c5124cb180790bf726e62cca792cb300b -- exactly the digest dictionaries/MANIFEST.md records. Present since 67fd4f5, never deleted.

Nothing would have caught it: .gitignore covers only /dictionaries/*.dict; .dockerignore has NO dictionary entry, so the file sits in every build context (the current image is clean only because the Dockerfile COPYs explicit paths); ARCH-FW-1 matches the three firmware manifest entries and the U202 magic only.

title: [TASK-6.13] Five days in eight arm the listings PID and program no title filter
description:
Measured 2026-09-20 sweeping eight consecutive days (MJD 50873..50880) with a TOT. On MJD mod 8 in {1,3,6} the box programs a title match unit within ~430k instructions. On {0,2,4,5,7} it arms the correct listings PID (0x30 | mjd%8, which is right on all eight days) and then programs NO title match unit at all within 200M instructions -- there is nothing in between, so it is not a timeout. A box with an armed PID and no filter receives nothing, so five days in eight cannot currently be fed listings.

Evidence and the unconditional 16-unit dumps: docs/reference/digibox-emulation.md -> 'The clock table is the TOT, and the listings PID is a day-of-eight rotation'.

Until this is understood the in-world clock (TASK-6.7) cannot choose an arbitrary day: it must land on a slot the box subscribes on, or the guide is empty for no visible reason.

-> /go-engineer
[TC-6.13]
spec: plan/phase-6-broadcast.md
notes:
NEXT STEP, so it is not re-derived. The symptom is NOT delivery: programmes register on all eight days (TestTheBoxTakesProgrammesAddressedFromTheClockAlone, 67 of 67 on slots 0,2,4,5,7). They are stored and not DRAWN, so the question is about the guide's read path, not the broadcast.

THE LEAD is the record's 'the guide is a SUBSCRIBER, not a reader': it registers a 44-byte notification slot and the notify fires only when service, day key and tableId&3 all match. sky-02me.5 observed the banner path registering two slots always reading 'service 0, day 50814, tidLow 2' -- note tidLow 2, while this transmitter sends table 0xA3, whose low bits are 3. Whether that matters is unmeasured.

WHAT TO BUILD FIRST: an instrument that locates and dumps the notification slot from DRAM on a running box, then read it on a DRAWING day (MJD mod 8 in 1,3,6 -- e.g. 51171, Christmas Eve 1998) and on a NON-DRAWING one (e.g. 51172), with everything else identical. If the slot is absent or differs on the non-drawing day, that is the answer. The oracle has __slots() for this; the Go port does not, and porting it is the same shape as the other instrument ports.

DO NOT re-measure delivery. That is settled and the tests pin it.

ANSWERED, and the task's own title was wrong: nothing about it was a day-of-eight problem. A day of listings is broadcast in FOUR SIX-HOUR BLOCKS and the low two bits of the title table id say which. The guide registers its notification slot for the block its own clock is in -- 00:00-05:59 -> 0, 06:00-11:59 -> 1, 12:00-17:59 -> 2, 18:00-23:59 -> 3, read off the box at eleven times of one day with the edges pinned at 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 -- and 0x800C579C wakes it only when the arriving section's tableId&3 matches. The transmitter stamped every section 0xA3, so it filed a whole day of television in the evening block: at 19:00 the guide drew it and at every other hour the box stored all 67 programmes and drew FURTHER SCHEDULE INFORMATION IS NOT AVAILABLE. The demo pins 19:00, which is why it presented as 'three days in eight' -- the correlation was real and incidental.

The bead's own lead was eliminated first and that is worth keeping: the slot is IDENTICAL on a drawing day and a non-drawing one (both day=clock's day, tableIdLow 3 at 19:00), so comparing two evening days could never have found this. Varying the hour did.

BUILT: multiplex.GuideSlots/GuideSubscription (the Go port of the oracle's __siGuideSlot, with the active flag read as the BYTE it is -- as a word every live slot reads inactive); QuarterOf/TitleTableID and a day emitted as four sections per channel, each stamped with its own block; and multiplex.TitlePID, because an evening box arms TWO listings PIDs and the old 'last armed PID' sent the whole schedule to tomorrow's PID on MJD mod 8 == 7 (0 of 67 registered, no error anywhere).

VERIFIED AT THE SCREEN, which is what TC-6.13 asked for. Two different titles must draw two different frames: they now do at 00:30, 06:00, 11:00, 12:00, 17:00, 18:00, 19:00 and 23:00, and on all eight day-slots at midday where before the fix NONE of them drew. Committed as TestTheOnAirTitleReachesTheScreenOutsideTheEveningBlock and TestTheGuideSubscribesForTheBlockOfTheDayItIsIn, plus unit tests for the block edges and the PID rotation.
